Taysha Gene Therapies Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update

11-12-2026   |  

PDF Version

REVEAL pivotal and ASPIRE trials evaluating TSHA-102 for Rett syndrome ongoing; expect to report topline data from 6-month interim analysis and FDA feedback on BLA submission pathway in 1H 2027

TSHA-102 continues to be generally well tolerated with no severe treatment-related SAEs or DLTs across REVEAL Phase 1/2, pivotal and ASPIRE trials (N=33) as of the November 2026 data cutoff

Completed BLA-enabling PPQ manufacturing campaign for TSHA-102, which met predefined product specifications as well as comparability criteria for commercial product and clinical material, supporting potential inclusion of REVEAL Part A Phase 1/2 data in the planned BLA

Encore data supporting TSHA-102 clinical program presented at the 55^{th} Child Neurology Society Annual Meeting

Conference call and webcast today at 8:30 AM ET

DALLAS, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Taysha Gene Therapies, Inc. (Nasdaq: TSHA) (Taysha or the Company), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on advancing adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapies for severe monogenic diseases of the central nervous system (CNS), today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update.

“During the third quarter, we continued to make strong progress across our clinical, manufacturing and commercial readiness activities as we advance toward a potential BLA submission for TSHA-102,” said Sean P. Nolan, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Taysha. “With all patients dosed and having cleared the acute post-dosing safety monitoring period in our REVEAL pivotal and ASPIRE trials with no severe treatment-related serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities observed across all studies, our focus now turns to delivering a robust dataset to support our planned BLA submission and further establish the potential of TSHA-102 to address the significant unmet need in Rett syndrome. In parallel, we achieved an important manufacturing milestone with the successful completion of our BLA-enabling PPQ manufacturing campaign, which met the predefined acceptance and comparability criteria previously reviewed with FDA. Importantly, the results further demonstrated our ability to consistently manufacture high-quality product at commercial scale, including an encouraging single-digit empty capsid percentage, a key indicator of product quality that contributes to patient safety. Looking ahead, we believe the first half of 2027 could be a transformative period for Taysha with our plan to report data from the six-month interim analysis of our REVEAL pivotal trial along with expected FDA feedback on our BLA submission pathway, and the anticipated nomination of a second gene therapy development program with a high unmet medical need and robust commercial opportunity as we begin building a broader CNS genetic medicine franchise.”

Recent Corporate and TSHA-102 Program Highlights

  * REVEAL Pivotal and ASPIRE Trials Ongoing with TSHA-102 Continued to be Generally Well-Tolerated. High dose (1x10^{15} total vector genomes (vg)) and low dose (5.7x10^{14} total vg) TSHA-102 continue to be generally well tolerated with no severe treatment-related serious adverse events (SAEs) or dose limiting toxicities (DLTs) in all patients treated in the REVEAL Phase 1/2, REVEAL pivotal and ASPIRE trials (N=33) as of the November 2026 data cutoff. All patients in the REVEAL Phase 1/2 (n=12), pivotal (n=17) and ASPIRE (n=4) trials have cleared the acute post-dosing safety monitoring period typically associated with AAV gene therapies with no dose-limiting toxicities observed across all trials.
  * Completed BLA-Enabling Process Performance Qualification (PPQ) Campaign for TSHA-102. Following alignment on the company’s proposed PPQ strategy with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Taysha completed its Biologics License Application (BLA)-enabling PPQ manufacturing campaign for TSHA-102, including the successful production of commercial-scale drug product batches required to validate the final commercial manufacturing process in support of a potential BLA submission and future commercialization of TSHA-102.
    * All process parameters and analytical results met predefined product specifications as well as comparability criteria for commercial product and clinical material. Together with the comparability of the clinical material used across the REVEAL Part A and Part B pivotal trials, these results support the potential inclusion of REVEAL Part A data in the planned BLA submission.
    * The final TSHA-102 commercial manufacturing process consistently achieved a single-digit empty capsid percentage, an important indicator of product quality that contributes to patient safety. The PPQ results also demonstrate the process consistency and scalability required to support potential commercial demand. The Company plans to discuss these Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) data in an anticipated meeting with FDA in the fourth quarter of 2026 to further strengthen the CMC package for the potential BLA submission.
  * Showcased Multiple Encore Presentations Supporting TSHA-102 Clinical Program at the 55^{th} Child Neurology Society Annual Meeting. One oral presentation and three poster presentations were delivered at the 55^{th} Child Neurology Society Annual Meeting. The presentations, available on the Company’s website, highlighted data previously presented at the 2026 International Rett Syndrome Foundation (IRSF) Scientific Meeting.

Anticipated Milestones

  * FDA feedback following CMC Type B meeting expected in the first quarter of 2027
  * Topline data from the REVEAL pivotal trial 6-month interim analysis and FDA feedback on the BLA submission pathway for TSHA-102 expected in the first half of 2027
  * Expect to nominate an additional gene therapy development candidate targeting a CNS disorder with high unmet need and commence preclinical development activities in the first half of 2027

Taysha Gene Therapies Announces Completion of Dosing in REVEAL Pivotal Trial and Reports Longer-Term Clinical Data from Part A of REVEAL Phase 1/2 Trials Evaluating TSHA-102 for Rett Syndrome

06-22-2026   |  

PDF Version

Completed dosing of 17 patients in REVEAL pivotal trial; topline data from 6‑month interim analysis and FDA feedback on next steps toward BLA submission pathway expected 1H 2027

TSHA-102 was generally well-tolerated with no treatment-related SAEs or DLTs reported as of the June 2026 data cutoff across REVEAL Phase 1/2 and pivotal trials (N=29)

100% of REVEAL Part A patients (N=12, 6-21 years) gained/regained ≥one developmental milestone by 12 months post-TSHA-102, with consistent responses across ages and disease severity

Longer-term follow‑up showed a durable and deepening treatment effect ≥12 months post-TSHA-102, with functional gains accumulating over time across core disease domains

310 total functional gains demonstrated ≥12 months post-TSHA-102 (~26 per patient), comprising 31 developmental milestones and 279 additional skill gains/improvements

Robust and clinically meaningful responses at both 6 and ≥12 months in REVEAL Part A further support potential for BLA submission based on REVEAL pivotal trial 6-month interim analysis

DALLAS, June 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Taysha Gene Therapies, Inc. (Nasdaq: TSHA) (Taysha or the Company), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on advancing adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapies for severe monogenic diseases of the central nervous system (CNS), today announced the completion of dosing in the REVEAL pivotal trial and reported positive longer-term clinical data from Part A of the REVEAL Phase 1/2 trials evaluating TSHA-102 for the treatment of Rett syndrome.

“As we advance toward a potential BLA submission for TSHA-102, we remain committed to developing a comprehensive, scientifically rigorous data package informed by our ongoing discussions with the FDA. We are pleased to report the completion of dosing in our REVEAL pivotal trial and positive longer-term follow-up data from our REVEAL Phase 1/2 trials. The data demonstrated early, durable treatment effect across all 12 pediatric, adolescent and adult patients, with responses continuing to deepen over time. On average, patients achieved 26 functional gains across core disease domains that impact activities of daily living at ≥12 months post-treatment, with consistent benefits observed regardless of age or disease severity,” said Sean P. Nolan, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Taysha.

Longer-Term Clinical Data from Part A of the REVEAL Phase 1/2 Adolescent/Adult and Pediatric Trials

REVEAL Part A efficacy data based on the May 2026 data cutoff included 12 females with Rett syndrome aged 6-21 years (high dose, n=8; low dose, n=4) treated with the high dose (1x10^{15} total vg) or low dose (5.7x10^{14} total vg) of TSHA-102, each with ≥12 months of follow-up

  * 100% of patients gained/regained ≥one developmental milestone across the core functional domains of fine motor, gross motor and communication post-TSHA-102 (i.e., spoke in phrases with meaning, used utensils to eat without assistance, walked with support), as assessed by multiple independent raters through video-evidenced evaluation
  * Longer-term follow‑up demonstrated a durable, deepening treatment effect across all patients, with additional functional gains continuing to accumulate over time through ≥12 months
    * Developmental milestone gains increased by 69% from 6 to 12 months and by 94% from 6 to ≥12 months post-TSHA-102

As of November 2026, TSHA-102 was generally well tolerated with no severe treatment-related serious adverse events, or SAEs, or dose limiting toxicities, or DLTs, in all patients treated in the REVEAL Phase 1/2, REVEAL pivotal and ASPIRE trials (n=33). In July 2026, one patient in the REVEAL pivotal trial experienced a single, moderate Grade 2 technical classification of a treatment-related event of peripheral sensory neuropathy, an expected AAV-associated risk, approximately six weeks post-TSHA-102. In accordance with the treating institution’s protocol, the patient was admitted overnight for management and observation, thus, resulting in the technical classification of the Grade 2 event as an SAE. The patient was discharged the following day, and importantly, rapidly demonstrated substantial recovery. The patient has demonstrated continued meaningful improvement over the last three months and is almost back to baseline.

Developmental milestones are defined as a functional gain of one or more of the 28 milestones defined in the natural history study. This is the primary evidence of efficacy that will support our planned BLA submission and the FDA’s review of efficacy in the REVEAL pivotal trial. In the REVEAL Part A trial, developmental milestones were assessed by multiple independent raters through video-evidenced evaluation.

The 12 patients treated in REVEAL Part A ranged from 6 to 21 years of age at dosing, with post-treatment follow-up spanning 12 to 30 months. We enrolled patients across a broad spectrum of disease severity, as assessed by the Clinical Global Impression-Severity, or CGI-S, scale, a 7-point, clinician-rated assessment of illness severity ranging from 1 (normal/not at all ill) to 7 (among the most extremely ill). Baseline scores ranged from 4 to 6, reflecting moderately to severely ill patients.
